function: Joint learned control of HAP beamforming, UAV-mounted RIS phase shifts, power-splitting ratio, public-stream rate and UAV trajectory to maximize energy efficiency of a RIS-RSMA satellite-aerial relay (pp. 7-8).
system: GEO satellite (16 antennas) to HAP over FSO; HAP (64 antennas) to 30 single-antenna devices via 2 UAV-mounted reflecting RISs (M=10), 2.4 GHz, 15 MHz (pp. 3, 11).
method: Federated DRL: LSTM-augmented DDQN agents trained per UAV, weights averaged at the HAP; global DDQN moves the UAV, local DDQN sets beams, RIS phases, power split (pp. 7-10).
data_channel: Own simulator: FSO Gamma-Gamma turbulence (satellite-HAP), Nakagami-m direct link, Rician HAP-RIS, quasi-static block fading RIS-device with path loss; GEO, 2.4 GHz; no dataset (pp. 5-6, 11).
test_conditions: Agents trained and evaluated in the same simulated environment (K=30, U=2); sweeps over HAP antennas, power, devices, RIS elements; no unseen-scenario test (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Non-learned: MRT beamforming, alternating-optimization (AO) scheme. Learned: partitioning DRL scheme inspired by [70]; centralized OMA, NOMA and RSMA DRL; SDMA, NOMA and no-RIS variants (pp. 11-13).
metrics: Energy efficiency, cumulative reward, UAV trajectory; sum-rate and power-consumption objectives compared through energy efficiency (pp. 12-13).
complexity: Per-agent order O(|Dm| + n_lay n_tra I |D_stp|); action-space sizes of local, global and centralized DRL compared analytically; no runtime or FLOPs (pp. 10-11).
q1_support: p. 5: "we can simply model the mentioned channel G [n] as Rician". Own simulator: Nakagami-m direct link, Gamma-Gamma FSO, quasi-static block fading, parameters in Table II (p. 11); no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data is named.
q2_support: p. 11: "We consider the scenario with K = 30 ground devices". One scenario; Figs. 4-7 sweep HAP antennas, power, devices, RIS elements; no trained policy is tested in an unseen scenario and no fine-tuning or transfer is reported.
q3_support: p. 11: "Partitioning Scheme: Inspired by [70], in this scheme,". Learned: partitioning scheme (earlier DRL [70]) and NOMA DRL like [68]; non-learned: MRT and AO schemes (pp. 11-12); compared on energy efficiency in Fig. 4 (p. 12).
q4_support: p. 10: "The computational complexity of each agent primarily" depends on transformations and backpropagation, given as O(|Dm| + n_lay n_tra I |D_stp|); action-space sizes compared with centralized DRL (pp. 10-11).
q5_support: p. 11: "Moreover, the system model parameters and neural network" hyper-parameters are listed in Table II; no link, DOI, repository or data-availability statement, and the data are simulated, not public.
notes: Included as area 6: the local DDQN action holds RIS phase changes, beamforming changes, power-splitting ratio and public-stream rate (p. 8, Eq. 33) with UAV moves from the global agent (p. 7), so a physical-layer decision is learned. The federated step averages DRL weights at the HAP (p. 9), not over the air, so area 7 does not apply. q3 is a judgment: the centralized RSMA DRL is a variant of the proposed method and is not counted; the partitioning scheme is only described as inspired by [70], and the NOMA DRL as like [68]; reviewer to confirm. Table II was read as a page image; its episode count (10000) differs from the text (1x10^6, p. 11).
